title: FRP Panels
short_answer: A plastic panel glued to a wall — punishes two mistakes: a substrate that is not flat, and not leaving room for the panel to move.
summary: FRP is a tough plastic sheet glued flat to the wall with trim at joints. The wall behind it must be genuinely flat, and you must leave expansion gaps or panels buckle.
plain_words: FRP is a tough plastic sheet, glued flat to the wall, with plastic trim covering the joints. It goes in kitchens, restrooms and anywhere that gets hosed down. Two things decide whether it looks right: the wall behind it has to be genuinely flat, and you have to leave gaps at the edges, because the panels grow and shrink. Butt them tight and they buckle.
when_to_use: Kitchen, restroom, and washdown FRP panel installs per submittal
After substrate is verified flat and adhesive-rated
Before pricing — confirm GVC scope inclusions first
prerequisites: Manufacturer installation guide for the specified FRP line
Substrate flatness verified (furring over CMU when needed)
Scope confirmed: furnish vs install-only, substrate prep, sealant ownership

materials.name: Adhesive rated for substrate and panel
Furring and substrate over CMU when required

steps.title: Acclimate
steps.body: Acclimate panels in the space they will be installed, flat, per manufacturer's stated period.

steps.title: String the wall
steps.body: String or straightedge the wall. Level high and low spots first — this is the step that gets skipped.

steps.title: Substrate ready
steps.body: Confirm substrate is adhesive-rated, clean, dry, and free of dust and debris that would break the bond.

steps.title: Layout
steps.body: Plan layout so joints land sensibly and you do not finish on a sliver.

steps.title: Dry-fit
steps.body: Dry-fit and mark every penetration — fixtures, outlets, plumbing — before adhesive is on anything.

steps.title: Adhesive coverage
steps.body: 100% coverage on panel back in cross-hatch with specified trowel. Roll from center outward with laminate roller.

steps.title: Expansion gaps
steps.body: Typical 4×8 panel: minimum 1/4" gap top and bottom, 1/8" between panels, clearance at penetrations and molding stem — confirm manufacturer instructions.

steps.title: Moldings and silicone
steps.body: Silicone in every molding channel; in washdown areas, silicone moldings to floor and ceiling as well.

steps.title: Done checks
steps.body: No bubbles (sound the face), gaps present, silicone continuous, moldings straight, faces clean, film removed.

warnings.title: Uneven substrate
warnings.body: On CMU or brick, furring with suitable substrate — not FRP straight onto masonry. A wavy wall reads as a wavy glossy wall.

warnings.title: No expansion allowance
warnings.body: FRP moves with temperature and humidity. Panels installed tight buckle outward — gaps are not optional.

warnings.title: Scope question for GVC
warnings.body: FRP is title-only in the portal estimate scope catalog. Before pricing, confirm: furnish panels and trim or install owner-furnished material; who prepares substrate; who owns sealant work. Those three answers change the number substantially.

experts.summary: Adhesive: 100% cross-hatch coverage, laminate roll from center out, respect open time. Expansion: typical 1/4" top/bottom and 1/8" between panels on 4×8 — manufacturer governs. Moldings: silicone in channel for moisture resistance; 1/8" between panel edge and molding stem. Cutting: fine-tooth blade face-up; support fully; penetrations slightly generous. Incomplete adhesive contact causes permanent bubbles.

variations.title: CMU / masonry substrate
changes: Furring strips with suitable substrate over masonry
Never glue FRP directly to uneven CMU

variations.title: Washdown areas
changes: Silicone moldings to floor and ceiling
Water behind panel cannot be inspected later

quality_checks.prompt: Substrate stringed and leveled before adhesive
Full adhesive contact — no hollow spots when sounded
Expansion gaps at top, bottom, between panels, and penetrations
Silicone continuous in molding channels (washdown: floor/ceiling too)

common_mistakes.title: Skip flatness prep
common_mistakes.wrong: Glue FRP over wavy CMU or high spots
common_mistakes.right: Fur, substrate, string and shim first

common_mistakes.title: Butt panels tight
common_mistakes.wrong: No gap at joints or perimeter
common_mistakes.right: Manufacturer expansion gaps at every edge

common_mistakes.title: Starved adhesive
common_mistakes.wrong: Spot glue or incomplete trowel coverage
common_mistakes.why: Bubbles cannot be fixed — panel comes off

troubleshooting.symptom: Hollow spot or bubble in panel face
troubleshooting.fix: Remove and replace panel — bubbles are not repairable in place

troubleshooting.symptom: Panel bowed off wall at joint
troubleshooting.fix: Remove affected panels; reinstall with correct gaps per manufacturer

provenance.note: Substrate flatness, 100% cross-hatch adhesive, laminate rolling, silicone in molding channels, and typical 1/4" / 1/8" expansion gaps for 4×8 panels come from published FRP manufacturer guides (Crane Composites, Glasliner, Marlite and similar). Product-specific numbers govern. Scope question for GVC: FRP is title-only in the estimate scope catalog — confirm furnish vs install-only, substrate prep ownership, and sealant work before pricing.
